0b9a5b2d707c.speaker: Scroll
0b9a5b2d707c.text: The MHC molecules wait empty. First the ribosome to the south must build the antigen protein.

11a88a25cb51.speaker: Scroll
11a88a25cb51.text: The tumor antigen is displayed on the cell surface by an MHC molecule. T-cells inspect it, recognize it, and multiply into an army that hunts any cell wearing the same antigen.

ba8904b6fe43.speaker: Arin
ba8904b6fe43.text: But the T-cells that must learn this face gather elsewhere... in the lymph nodes. Let's go.

8d0d74039d76.speaker: Scroll
8d0d74039d76.text: The antigen is displayed on the cell surface. Now the dendritic cell must carry it to a lymph node — the way lies north.

819f7adfb833.speaker: Scroll
819f7adfb833.text: Hurry! In the cytoplasm, deadenylases nibble the poly(A) tail from the 3' end. When the tail is gone the mRNA loses its cap and is destroyed.

88f85f96977d.speaker: Scroll
88f85f96977d.text: Reach the ribosome before the tail runs out. Exonucleases patrol the path — leap over them!

34a516a6b1c8.speaker: Scroll
34a516a6b1c8.text: Without its tail the mRNA was decapped and destroyed. Another copy escapes the endosome — run straight for the ribosome and leap over the exonucleases!

b7d23be8d6d4.speaker: Scroll
b7d23be8d6d4.text: The exonucleases chewed the mRNA to pieces. Another copy escapes the endosome — this time, leap over them!

35d282448359.speaker: Scroll
35d282448359.text: A voice echoes: 'Brave Arin... the Princess waits beyond. Hurry.'

7a457882ded3.speaker: Scroll
7a457882ded3.text: The dendritic cell has nothing to show yet. It must first present the antigen on MHC.

42d2b2afe194.speaker: Scroll
42d2b2afe194.text: The dendritic cell carries the antigen on its surface. Now it must travel to a lymph node, where the T-cells gather.

ea51428cea5e.speaker: Arin
ea51428cea5e.text: How does it know the way?

54b4d16b463d.speaker: Scroll
54b4d16b463d.text: It smells its way. The lymph node releases a chemokine, CCL19. The cell raises CCR7 antennae and crawls toward the stronger scent.

cd57ae5cb631.speaker: Scroll
cd57ae5cb631.text: Carried by the lymph, the dendritic cell reaches the lymph node. Inside, thousands of naive T-cells wait, each with a different receptor.

f4400f58fef3.speaker: Arin
f4400f58fef3.text: One of them must fit our antigen. Let's find it.

0287fb4ddd1d.speaker: Scroll
0287fb4ddd1d.text: The dendritic cell has already reached the lymph node. Enter the T-cell zone to the north.

ce7ccac62f1c.speaker: Scroll
ce7ccac62f1c.text: The dendritic cell drifts in the tissue. Follow the CCL19 scent with the CCR7 antennae to reach the vessel.

5fe02afc9249.speaker: Cell
5fe02afc9249.text: I am a dendritic cell. I reach out with my branches and capture particles... but you carry nothing for me yet.

cfa3d69e08ff.speaker: Arin
cfa3d69e08ff.text: The Lipid Nanoparticle — I must bring it here first.

e956067a2db6.speaker: Cell
e956067a2db6.text: I am a dendritic cell — a sentinel of the immune system. I captured your nanoparticle and drew it inside an endosome.

6dec79fc449f.speaker: Scroll
6dec79fc449f.text: This is endocytosis: the membrane folds around the particle and pinches off as a vesicle. The mRNA is now inside the cell, but still trapped in the endosome.

89717d92a59d.speaker: Arin
89717d92a59d.text: Then the next step is to break free. Onward, to the endosome!

b2d4b0eefdca.speaker: Cell
b2d4b0eefdca.text: The nanoparticle is already inside me, sealed in an endosome. Follow it north — the endosome is turning acidic.

352186b7f88a.speaker: Scroll
352186b7f88a.text: This endosome is empty. The nanoparticle must first be captured by the dendritic cell to the south.

ca00e7561ae8.speaker: Scroll
ca00e7561ae8.text: Inside the endosome the pH dropped. The ionizable lipids became positively charged, disrupted the membrane, and the vesicle burst open.

c6521d7df417.speaker: Arin
c6521d7df417.text: The mRNA escapes through the torn membrane into the cytoplasm — free at last!

57cc75d85e98.speaker: Scroll
57cc75d85e98.text: Now the ribosomes can read it. Head north — but hurry, the cytoplasm is full of nucleases.

3dcdac4ac58c.speaker: Scroll
3dcdac4ac58c.text: The mRNA has already escaped this endosome. The ribosome to the north is waiting to translate it.

2243bd59a1cd.speaker: Scroll
2243bd59a1cd.text: The mRNA was digested. Endosomal escape is a race: wait for the lipids to charge (pH below 6.6), but break out before pH 5, when the lysosome fuses.

5d9fc4dd01fc.speaker: Arin
5d9fc4dd01fc.text: The cell is taking in more particles. Let me try again.

77af09628413.speaker: Scroll
77af09628413.text: The endosome is acidifying. Watch the pH: the lipids only charge below pH 6.6, and below pH 5 the lysosome arrives. Tap or press SPACE at the right moment to break out.

e61d39f66deb.speaker: Scroll
e61d39f66deb.text: No army has been raised yet. The T-cells must first be activated in the lymph node.

3be9c2eb2f92.speaker: Scroll
3be9c2eb2f92.text: The activated T-cells ride the blood and squeeze out of the vessel here, drawn by the tumor's chemokines. But the tumor defends itself.

411aeceead59.speaker: Scroll
411aeceead59.text: Regulatory T-cells breathe out IL-10 and TGF-beta that switch fighters off. Cancer-associated fibroblasts wall the tumor in with dense collagen. Hypoxic pockets sap their strength.

04e6a248321f.speaker: Arin
04e6a248321f.text: Then I'll lead them myself. Stay close, all of you!

c517dded9b10.speaker: Scroll
c517dded9b10.text: The T-cells have infiltrated the tumor. Now each one must read the cells around it and choose its target.

2fa3013c52ac.speaker: Scroll
2fa3013c52ac.text: The army is inside the tumor. Head north and begin the hunt.

d5d7fb446e9c.speaker: Scroll
d5d7fb446e9c.text: Too few T-cells reached the tumor. Keep the herd close, steer them around the purple Treg fog, and find the gaps in the stroma.

ecdb07f2c86c.speaker: Scroll
ecdb07f2c86c.text: Beware! The naked mRNA is out, and RNases — enzymes that shred unprotected RNA — are prowling the kingdom.

b8e2b5d5114e.speaker: Scroll
b8e2b5d5114e.text: Three bites and the message is gone. Leap over them with SPACE or the JUMP button, and get the mRNA to the mixer!

b66ba8b2289f.speaker: Arin
b66ba8b2289f.text: Then I'll be quick on my feet.

f658ccfd0307.speaker: Synthesizer
f658ccfd0307.text: The message was destroyed by RNase. Here is a fresh copy — this time, leap over them!

d43833a73bbe.speaker: Mixer
d43833a73bbe.text: Nothing to encapsulate yet. Assemble the mRNA at the synthesizer first.

79fc37a492c8.speaker: Scroll
79fc37a492c8.text: Naked mRNA would be shredded in the blood within minutes. It needs a shield: a lipid nanoparticle.

26aaf72b2a0b.speaker: Mixer
26aaf72b2a0b.text: I am a microfluidic mixer. Feed lipids in ethanol into one inlet and the mRNA in acidic buffer into the other, and my herringbone channel folds them together in milliseconds.

ed9c76123f10.speaker: Mixer
ed9c76123f10.text: Batch complete: small, uniform nanoparticles with the mRNA safely inside, now at neutral pH.

27f551e260fb.speaker: Scroll
27f551e260fb.text: The shielded message is ready. Take it to the injection gate — Mira's body awaits.

f9bb4b3b64a9.speaker: Mixer
f9bb4b3b64a9.text: The LNP batch is ready. Head to the injection gate on the right.

d2a2bcfdd212.speaker: Mixer
d2a2bcfdd212.text: No batch yet. Load both inlets, set the flow ratio to 3:1 with a fast total flow, run, then exchange the buffer.

2fb7be2b0d37.speaker: Mira
2fb7be2b0d37.text: Arin... you came. But I am gravely ill. The healers call it cancer.

ca0be7ec8a3f.speaker: Arin
ca0be7ec8a3f.text: I will not lose you. There must be a cure.

7494c9044174.speaker: Mira
7494c9044174.text: On the pedestal... an ancient scroll. It speaks of a strange medicine.

a6c7d5052be0.speaker: Scroll
a6c7d5052be0.text: To teach the body to fight the illness, craft an mRNA — a message of life.

2ab753aa728a.speaker: Scroll
2ab753aa728a.text: Gather its seven parts: 5′ cap, 5′ UTR, start codon, the antigen code, stop codon, 3′ UTR, and poly(A) tail.

b33520a740d6.speaker: Scroll
b33520a740d6.text: Assemble them, wrap them in a lipid shield, and deliver the message within.

5a856b354a86.speaker: Arin
5a856b354a86.text: Then to the molecular kingdom I go. Hold on, Mira.

310edac9b527.speaker: Ribosome
310edac9b527.text: I am a ribosome, but I have nothing to read. The mRNA is still trapped inside the endosome to the south.

d2dcf7e9cf69.speaker: Ribosome
d2dcf7e9cf69.text: I read the message three letters at a time — each codon calls for one amino acid — and linked them into a chain.

b078f6102d02.speaker: Scroll
b078f6102d02.text: The chain folds into the tumor antigen: a harmless copy of a protein found on Mira's cancer cells. Now the cell can show it to the immune system.

f24b2cfba496.speaker: Arin
f24b2cfba496.text: So the body learns the enemy's face without ever meeting the enemy. On to the surface!

ebfaea8b0077.speaker: Ribosome
ebfaea8b0077.text: The antigen is made. Carry on north — the cell is presenting it on its surface now.

5c1c1781898f.speaker: Synthesizer
5c1c1781898f.text: The mRNA is ready. Take it to the microfluidic mixer to wrap it in a lipid nanoparticle.

2d3e83ad23de.speaker: Scroll
2d3e83ad23de.text: The T-cell zone is sealed. The dendritic cell must first arrive through the lymphatic vessel.

ca7dba5a815e.speaker: Scroll
ca7dba5a815e.text: Naive T-cells. Each carries one unique T-cell receptor, a TCR. Only a receptor shaped to fit our antigen on MHC can recognise it.

c7a7ea9d9319.speaker: Arin
c7a7ea9d9319.text: Like a key and a lock. Let the dendritic cell show the antigen, and we test them one by one.

b1f00ba2a91d.speaker: Scroll
b1f00ba2a91d.text: The matching T-cell locked onto the antigen, received its three signals, and multiplied into an army of identical fighters.

59bfcea3803d.speaker: Arin
59bfcea3803d.text: Every one of them knows the face of Mira's cancer.

44e275cc1c49.speaker: Mira
44e275cc1c49.text: Arin... I can feel my strength returning. The message you delivered has become an army. Thank you.

f5428fe0e659.speaker: Scroll
f5428fe0e659.text: The T-cell army is on the march. Follow them north, out through the efferent lymph toward the tumor.

5ac08fd854be.speaker: Scroll
5ac08fd854be.text: No T-cell was activated. Compare each TCR's notches with the antigen key and test the one that fits.

fefb21dc4a88.speaker: Mira
fefb21dc4a88.text: Arin! The fever is gone... I can stand again. The healers say the growth has vanished.

184a9daae835.speaker: Arin
184a9daae835.text: Your own body did it, Mira. We only taught it the enemy's face — with a message written in mRNA.

7af06e9c1b34.speaker: Mira
7af06e9c1b34.text: A message of life. Then let the whole kingdom learn to read it.

77d28d00077b.speaker: Scroll
77d28d00077b.text: Colour returns to the princess's face. The prince steps out of her body at last... and the two of them kiss.

57a8fc02da4a.speaker: Scroll
57a8fc02da4a.text: Some of the T-cells stay behind as memory cells: if the illness ever returns, they will remember its face. And so the secret of the scroll was shared. THE END.

23a0f75e94d5.speaker: Scroll
23a0f75e94d5.text: The T-cells are still in the blood. Lead them out of the vessel to the south and through the stroma first.

e15d2e7cf808.speaker: Scroll
e15d2e7cf808.text: The T-cells that made it through the stroma are inside the tumor now.

77f715612e2a.speaker: Arin
77f715612e2a.text: So many cells... how will they know which ones to strike?

e80119f9b5f3.speaker: Scroll
e80119f9b5f3.text: Every cell shows pieces of its inner proteins on MHC class I. Tumor cells show the vaccine antigen; healthy cells show only self. The T-cell reads each one before it strikes.

307a604204dc.speaker: Scroll
307a604204dc.text: Beware: some tumor cells wear PD-L1, a checkpoint that switches T-cells off. A checkpoint-inhibitor antibody can remove that disguise.

7206a1d187ef.speaker: Scroll
7206a1d187ef.text: The tumor is gone. Perforin opened the way, granzymes did the work, and every tumor cell died by apoptosis — while the healthy cells were untouched.

4ff065d60f5a.speaker: Scroll
4ff065d60f5a.text: Some of the T-cells become memory cells. If the cancer ever returns, they will remember its face.

e7cca321aa5e.speaker: Arin
e7cca321aa5e.text: Mira... it is over. Let's go home.

35e5f78dc4df.speaker: Scroll
35e5f78dc4df.text: The tumor has been destroyed. Mira waits to the north.

f3dc0a0fcadb.speaker: Scroll
f3dc0a0fcadb.text: The tumor still grows. Read each cell's MHC-I peptide: strike the vaccine antigen, spare self — and grab the antibody to beat PD-L1.

fb0085a7ba5c.speaker: Scroll
fb0085a7ba5c.text: Protects the mRNA and helps ribosomes find the start.

948c4c563265.speaker: Scroll
948c4c563265.text: Untranslated region that tunes how efficiently mRNA is read.

87c0635fc451.speaker: Scroll
87c0635fc451.text: Open reading frame coding the tumor antigen.

af2954c58408.speaker: Scroll
af2954c58408.text: Signals the ribosome to release the finished protein.

38649d256c86.speaker: Scroll
38649d256c86.text: A tail of adenines that stabilizes the mRNA.

bbfefcbe06a0.speaker: Scroll
bbfefcbe06a0.text: Delivery vehicle that protects and carries the mRNA.

81d91e798c0d.speaker: Scroll
81d91e798c0d.text: Immune protein that recognizes the presented antigen.

5b58ca670833.speaker: Scroll
5b58ca670833.text: Molecular machine that reads mRNA into protein.

6ee611ab749e.text: The gate is sealed. Collect all 7 components and operate the Synthesizer first.

0157d58542d2.text: The way is not open yet.

c9627bea09c1.speaker: Scroll
c9627bea09c1.text:
STEP 1 - Load the two inlets.

Ethanol inlet (left): all four lipids - the ionizable lipid, DSPC, cholesterol and the PEG-lipid. Lipids are hydrophobic, so they only dissolve in ethanol.

pH 4 acetate buffer inlet (right): the mRNA. It is water-soluble and must never sit in the ethanol.

The classic recipe dissolves about 50% ionizable lipid, 10% DSPC, 38.5% cholesterol and 1.5% PEG-lipid (molar ratio) in the ethanol stream. Drag every tile to its inlet, then press F1 again for the flow settings.

54f9c83f998a.speaker: Scroll
54f9c83f998a.text:
STEP 2 - The ideal formulation.

Flow-rate ratio (buffer : ethanol) = 3 : 1. Set the first slider to 3.0 (anything from 2.5 to 3.5 passes). Three volumes of acidic mRNA buffer per one volume of lipid-ethanol dilutes the ethanol so quickly that the lipids precipitate around the mRNA as small particles of about 80 nm. With less buffer the particles fuse and grow; with more, the lipids precipitate unevenly.

Total flow rate: at least 10 mL/min. Push the second slider to 12 to 16. Fast flow lets the herringbone grooves mix the two streams in milliseconds, before the lipids can clump, which gives a low PDI and over 90% of the mRNA encapsulated.

Why pH 4: the ionizable lipid is positively charged in the acidic buffer, so it grabs the negatively charged mRNA while the particle forms.

Watch the 'Predicted' line: aim for about 80 nm, PDI below 0.10 and over 90% encapsulated, then press Run mixer.

4ea8c2b57270.speaker: Scroll
4ea8c2b57270.text:
STEP 3 - Finish the particle.

The batch is good. Press 'Exchange buffer to pH 7.4': dialysis removes the ethanol and raises the pH, so the ionizable lipid turns neutral and the LNP is gentle in the blood. It will only turn positive again inside the acidic endosome, where it must release the mRNA.

3b2d3709da47.speaker: Scroll
3b2d3709da47.text: The mixer is running. The two streams meet in the herringbone channel and fold together; at pH 4 the charged ionizable lipid captures the mRNA and the lipids precipitate into nanoparticles. Wait for the result, then press F1 again if you need the settings.

8d21eac0c912.speaker: Scroll
8d21eac0c912.text:
How to find the right T-cell.

Look at the orange antigen key sitting on the MHC of the dendritic cell: four bumps, from left to right medium, tall, short, medium.

Every naive T-cell hangs a blue receptor plate (its TCR) below it with four notches. Only one plate has notches of exactly those depths in the same order: medium, tall, short, medium. That plate would swallow the key perfectly.

To test a cell: tap it, or move the yellow ring with the left and right keys (or A and D) and press E. A wrong cell is only crossed out and greyed; you cannot lose, so keep testing until one fits.

Still unsure? When you close this clue, the matching T-cell glows green for a few seconds.

ff8ae4cd9ea6.speaker: Scroll
ff8ae4cd9ea6.text: The chosen T-cell is docking on the dendritic cell. Signal 1 is the TCR gripping the antigen on MHC. Signal 2 is CD28 meeting CD80/86. Signal 3 is the IL-12 cytokine. With all three, the T-cell activates and clones itself into an army.
